text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet and the International Monetary Fund announced an accord on financial reform and funding worth more than $650 million and an introduction of a currency board system in June to stabilise the country's economy. @
-- The caretaker cabinet is expected to raise wages in the public sector by 70 percent from April 1, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said.
-- The interim government cancelled the 1997 privatisation programme of the previous Socialist cabinet, saying the programme should reflect priorities included in the financial accord with the IMF.
-- Bulgaria is negotiating a barter of $60 million worth of Iranian crude oil for Bulgarian foods, a Trade ministry official said. @
-- The interim cabinet said customs officers should declare their incomes and property each year in a bid to fight corruption.
-- Bulgaria expects to receive some $300-350 million from privatisation deals this year, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.

-- Bulgaria's Agriculture minister Roumen Hristov left for a meeting of agriculture ministers from EU member countries and EU associate members in Brussels where a delivery of 100,000 tonnes of grain to Bulgaria is expected to be discussed. @
-- Bulgaria's domestic debt rose to 2.778 trillion levs at end-February from 1.678 trillion levs a month earlier, Finance ministry figures showed.

-- Belgium's Union Miniere, Swiss Glencore and South Korea's Lucky Goldstar were interested in buying a 56 percent stake in the Bulgarian copper smelter MDK Pirdop, the newspaper said without quoting sources. @
-- Bulgaria's private International Bank for Trade and Development decided to raise capital to 13 billion levs from 1.3 billion levs, the bank's executive director Alexander Alexandrov said.
-- Bulgaria's state-owned Hebros Bank said it had posted 15.4 billion levs profit last year after a 255 million levs loss for 1995.
